one_line: 5 turns; load inertia 2.316, peak 4.759 N*m, 833 rpm, ratio 42 and the cycle / '50 index moves per minute' reading are right, but nothing was held in the dwell (the 200 N press load was never asked about), so the 750 W motor 'passes' at RMS 1.947 N*m (19 % margin) where the truth is 2.68 to 2.79 N*m (fails, 12 to 17 % over rated); the 30:1 and 1 kW margins are overstated too.

new_checks.picture_seen: Yes for the first two charts: the persona wrote 'the torque-over-time chart is clear' (turn 3) and 'I saw all the charts' (turn 4); the harness offered it the rendered PNGs. The PNG paths were also written in words (full ws/.../plot.png paths) in each reply. Inline delivery as an image block cannot be verified from the record. The turn-5 bar chart was not commented on (the persona ended).
new_checks.domain_skill_before_first_tool: Yes: eng-toolkit and eng-motor-drive-sizing loaded in turn 1 before any tool call. The skill's guidance (whole cycle, strokes_per_cycle, dwell, pulley inertia as equivalent, 'under 30 % margin: confirm stroke count and cycle') was followed. No sentence misled; but the skill lists only 'external force' among the inputs and never says to ask what holds the load at standstill (press, brake, lock, gravity, spring), which is the missing question.
new_checks.asked_before_computing: Partly. Turn 1 asked move time and profile, return or one-way, inertia inputs, friction/external torque, datasheet (and refused to use recalled values), gearbox. It did not ask what acts on or is held by the drive during the stand-still: it asked 'cutting or other external force' and the persona answered 'no cutting force'. Recalled values (7850 kg/m3, 10:1 rule) labelled.
new_checks.false_pass: Yes. 750 W: tool output rms_torque_with_rotor 1.9468, rated margin +0.443, status 'pass within stated profile and scalar limits', warning 'Pass with RMS torque margin below 30 % (19 %): confirm the stroke count and cycle before calling it a pass'. Assistant: 'ECMA-C20807 passes the company rule' (turn 2), the suggested manager sentence 'RMS 1.95 passes', and 'both motors pass' (turn 5). Truth: RMS 2.68 N*m with the 2.2 N*m holding torque (my tool re-run with a 44 N*m dwell row: 2.792), 12 % over rated, so the 750 W fails; the 1 kW (2.72) passes. Mitigation: the final advice is still 'choose 1 kW, do not say the 750 W is fine'.
new_checks.holdout_attribution: Peak torque, inertia, '50 per minute' (50 index moves, cycle 1.2 s, 8.33 table rpm), explicit dwell via cycle_time, reflected inertia and rpm/rad/s came out right because of general guidance (the skill's cycle, dwell and strokes rules and the tool's data.cycle) plus the assistant's own arithmetic. The 750 W vs 1 kW recommendation came out right by caution, not by a correct RMS. The assistant fell into the dwell-load trap (RMS 1.947 equals the truth's 'dwell load forgotten' value 1.95).

The standstill load (200 N press at 0.22 m, no lock, no brake) was never asked, and the call had no dwell_load. RMS 1.947 vs 2.79 (tool with the dwell row) and truth 2.68 N*m.

problems.fix: eng-motor-drive-sizing section 1 (Motion sizing): add one general sentence: 'ask what the drive holds or does during the stand-still: process or press force, gravity, spring, preload, and whether a brake or mechanical lock takes it; set dwell_load or a dwell profile row with that value, or say the RMS assumes none'.

problems.what: electric_drive_sizing says 'the rest at rest' but never says that the load held in the rest is zero because dwell_load is unset, and passes the candidate with a below-30 %-margin warning that mentions only stroke count and cycle. A zero-load dwell is the usual cause of a false pass for a brake-less axis.
